p.title: v59.97 the Actions shared-AI client waits past the Worker's 60 s deadline for a non-search call
p.symptom: A non-search shared-AI request from GitHub Actions (market reading, headline translation fallback, slot summary) that took 30 to 60 s was aborted by the producer as provider-timeout, while the Worker, which allows that request 60 s, kept its full budget reservation for a response OpenAI may still complete and bill.
p.root_cause: SHARED_AI_TIMEOUT_MS.analysis was 30 s, shorter than the Worker's 60 s non-search deadline (openAiDeadlineMs); only the search timeout followed the rule that the client outwaits the Worker.
p.fix: SHARED_AI_TIMEOUT_MS.analysis is 65 s, a few seconds past the Worker's 60 s deadline, and the comment states the rule for both keys (60 s non-search, 120 s search).
p.violated_rule: A client timeout on a budgeted Worker call must outlast the Worker's own deadline so the Worker answers first.
p.prevention: ci-data-pipeline-contract-check v59.97 asserts SHARED_AI_TIMEOUT_MS.analysis > 60000 and search > 120000 (the Worker deadline constants are not exported, so the cross-file comparison is not made).
p.verification: node scripts/ci-data-pipeline-contract-check.mjs exit 0; the refresh job makes at most 4 analysis-timeout calls a run (headline translation fallback 1, market reading 1 + 1 retry, slot summary 1), a worst-case added wait of about 140 s against timeout-minutes 45.

changelog: **Actions AI client outwaits the Worker ({P}):** a non-search shared-AI call from the refresh job now waits 65 s instead of 30 s, past the Worker's 60 s deadline, so a slow answer is received instead of abandoned while its budget reservation stays held.
